shape_hint: A flat round annular washer: a thin disc with a concentric round hole, uniform thickness, both faces flat. N (SAE) pattern has a small outside diameter (about 2.2x hole), W (USS) pattern has a wide outside diameter (about 2.4-2.7x hole) and is thicker.

role_map.d_nom_note: nominal screw/bolt size; N = narrow series (SAE), W = wide series (USS); sizes #2-#12 and 3/16 have a single series, 1-5/8..3 in single series (wide pattern)

notes: ASME B18.21.1 (which absorbed B18.22.1) Type A plain washers, preferred sizes only, inch. 'N' = SAE and 'W' = USS in trade usage; the standard itself gives no separate N/W for sizes below 1/4 and above 1-1/2 (industry convention: small = SAE, 1-5/8 and larger = USS). OD 0.734 (1/4 W), 1.156 (9/16 N) and 1.469 (9/16 W, 3/4 N) are deliberate non-round values in the standard. Thickness 'h' is the basic value, tolerance via h_max/h_min. ID/OD tolerances (+0 to +0.045 on ID, +/- up to 0.010 on OD) are in the standard but are not published here. Type B washers and the fender washers are not included.

bhamfast: bhamfast.com SAE flat washer chart (narrow rows #4..1-1/2 only, ID/OD/T max/min with tolerances, no basic T)
JMET dataset: turn2engineering.com washer-size-chart (verified IDENTICAL on all 33 rows x 3 cols incl. the 7/16 SAE OD 15/16 error -> one source); fractions for ID/OD, decimal basic T; no max/min

verification.checks_done: Live re-fetch of ee, gf1111, bham, fastenersart, turn2, blueribbon, baden, nw/bestmat/brighton PDFs (gf1112 live=403, producer copy used only for context). Parsed ee (44 rows, own order mapping incl. 3 unlabelled rows -> #0/#2/#4), gf (44 columns over 3 table blocks), bham (21), JMET (33). Matrix 43 record rows x 5 value cols (d1,d2,h,h_max,h_min) x 4 non-PDF clusters (ee, gf, bham, JMET) with fractions accepted within 0.0006 (ASME decimals = round-half-even of the fraction). ee and gf agree with the record in ALL 215 cells (so max 2 clusters everywhere); bham adds the N rows #4..1-1/2 for d1,d2,h_max,h_min; JMET adds d1,d2,h for #2..2 (both series). Counted clusters: d1 >=3 except 3/16, 1-7/8, 2-1/4..3; d2 same; h >=3 except 3/16, 1-1/8N..1-1/2N, 1-7/8, 2 (JMET says 0.213, dissent), 2-1/4..3; h_max/h_min >=3 only for N rows #4..1 N (24 of 43 rows have only ee+gf: all W rows, #2, 3/16, 1-1/8N+, all single-series >= 1-5/8). Physical sanity (h_min<h<h_max, d2>d1, W>=N, monotone) fine.
problems: Producer's 3rd source for most rows was the northwestfastener.com PDF (and bestmaterials/brighton PDFs): vendor sheets are corroboration only, so ee+gf+PDF = 2 counted clusters.

h_max and h_min: only ee + gf (+bham for N rows #4..1 N). Every W row, #2, 3/16 and all rows >= 1-1/8 N have 2 counted clusters -> columns dropped (alternative: keep h_max/h_min and keep only the 15 rows #4,#6,#8,#10,#12 and 1/4 N..1 N; that loses the whole W series).

h (basic T): 3 clusters (ee, gf, JMET) for #2..#12, 1/4 N..1 N, all W rows to 1-1/2 W, 1-5/8, 1-3/4; only 2 for 3/16, 1-1/8 N..1-1/2 N (JMET has no SAE rows > 1 in), 1-7/8, 2, 2-1/4..3 -> rows dropped.

W-row d1/d2 rest on exactly 3 clusters (ee, gf, JMET) and JMET gives fractions (5/16 = 0.3125 vs 0.312, 1-15/32 vs 1.469); accepted as equal only because ASME's decimals are the round-half-even of the fraction. With zero tolerance the W rows' d1 would be 2 clusters.
7/16 N d2 = 0.922: ee, gf, bham agree; JMET/turn2 print 15/16 (0.9375), a dissenting error in that dataset (blueribbon/baden F436 fractions 59/64 support 0.922).

Row labels: '1/4 N' / '1/4 W' are unique and are the standard's own series letters (N = narrow, W = wide); the equation N = SAE, W = USS is trade convention (verified numerically against JMET's SAE/USS columns for every 1/4..1-1/2 row) and is NOT stated in the standard: recommend labelling '1/4 N (SAE)' / '1/4 W (USS)' or at least keeping the column note. Bare '1-5/8','1-3/4' (no series) are the standard's single-series rows (USS-like); the dropped bare '2' and '3' would be visually confusable with screw '#2'/'#3' -> if ever kept, label them in inches.

Label '#2' and '#4' are unlabelled ('-') in engineersedge and globalfastener; the label comes from JMET (and bham for #4) -> labels read from a header by 1 (#2) or 2 (#4) clusters, values by 3+. '#0' (ID 0.078) correctly excluded.
bhamfast 1-3/4 and 2 rows are F436-type numbers (OD 3.375/3.75), not Type A, and are ignored.

standard_full: ASME B18.21.1 Type A plain washers (preferred sizes; ex B18.22.1 Table 1A): N = narrow (SAE), W = wide (USS)
